evidence: The sole title, Liber Pontificalis Ecclesiae Ravennatis (2006 edition), is by the ninth-century Agnellus of Ravenna, also called Andreas Agnellus; Brepols explicitly identifies him as its author.
Newton Bignotto lists both Pensar a República (organizer) and Maquiavel (2003) among his books on his own profile. Neuton is a misspelling; both listed works belong to Newton.

A Mirror of England: English Puritan Views of Foreign Nations, 1618-1640 (1970), the sole listed work, is by Marvin Arthur Breslow, as confirmed by Google Books and the Cambridge-published review. Martin is a bibliographic error.

Consilium principis (1955) is by John Anthony Crook. The 1951 American Journal of Philology entry is identifiable as his article Titus and Berenice, 72(2):162-175; title fragments have been parsed into the author field. Both listed citations are his.

MIT Press credits Visual Culture: The Study of the Visual after the Cultural Turn (2005) to Margaret Dikovitskaya. Library records catalogue that same book under Margarita Dikovitskaya and explicitly recognize Margaret as a name variant.

Minnesota Historical Society Press identifies Rhoda R. Gilman, Carolyn Gilman and Deborah M. Stultz as authors of The Red River Trails (1979). Rhoda A and the coauthor surname Schulz are citation errors, with no second Rhoda represented.

Cambridge University Press identifies Keechang Kim as author of Aliens in Medieval Law: The Origins of Modern Citizenship (2000), the sole listed work. Ki-ch'ang is the corresponding catalogued romanization, also shown for the same book in Google Books.
Kitchener: Portrait of an Imperialist (1958) is by Sir Philip Magnus, born 1906; the publisher identifies him as Sir Philip Montefiore Magnus-Allcroft (1906-1988). Phillip is a spelling error.

National Polity and Local Power (1989) is by Min Tu-ki, edited by Philip A. Kuhn and Timothy Brook. Library MARC records explicitly pair the Min, Tu-gi heading with the title-page author Min Tu-ki; these are romanization variants.

Byzantium and Bulgaria, 775-831 is by Panos Sophoulis; library records explicitly catalogue that title under Pananos Sophoulis. The publisher preview also credits Bulgaria – “The New Byzantium” (2022), pp. 311-326, to Panos Sophoulis. Both listed works are his.
